verdict.rationale: Vercel documents its own CLI deploy flow (install, login, run `vercel`), which suggests deploying from a local project without Git. It also documents access protection for preview URLs and promoting a deployment to production, which together approximate a deployment kept private until published. Neither the no-Git folder upload nor a private-until-publish default is stated explicitly. missing for 10: explicit documentation that a local folder is uploaded directly without a Git repo, explicit confirmation that new deployments stay private/unpublished by default until promoted, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy a project by uploading a folder of files directly, with no Git repo required and the new deployment kept private until I choose to publish it

citations.quote: Deploy your app on Vercel in three steps: install the CLI, add agent support if you use an AI coding agent, and deploy.
Get started by importing a project, choosing a template, or using the Vercel CLI.
Control who can open your preview and production URLs with Vercel Authentication, passwords, or trusted IPs.
Send a new deployment to a percentage of traffic first, then promote it or roll back.
